_comment: What is actually stopping the transition in a sector, typed and sourced. A bottleneck
is not a risk register entry and not an opinion: it is a named constraint that at
least one technology addresses and at least one measure worsens or relieves, and the
edges saying so are what the sector diagram draws.
Schema and vocabularies: sources/sector_map.py. Gate: sources/check_sector_schema.py.
THE TYPE IS THE ARGUMENT. `technical` means no technology exists that removes the
constraint; `financial` means one exists and nobody will fund it; `infrastructure`
means one exists, is funded, and has nowhere to send its output; `market` means the
output exists and nobody will pay for it; `political` means the support it rests on is
revocable. A reader who disagrees with the type is disagreeing with something
specific, which is the point of typing it at all.
`description` states no number that is not in parameters.json. Where the quantification
is missing, `quantified_by` is short and data/transition/GAPS.md says what would fill
it — a bottleneck stated without a number is still a real constraint, and pretending
otherwise would push the file towards numbers nobody sourced.

bottlenecks.name: Process emissions from calcination
bottlenecks.description: The majority of a kiln's CO2 comes out of the limestone itself when it is calcined, not out of the fuel, so no amount of fuel switching or efficiency reaches it and capture is the only route that does.

sources.title: Cement — Energy System
World premiere at Heidelberg Materials: Opening of CCS facility in Norway

bottlenecks.name: CO2 transport and storage network
bottlenecks.description: A captured tonne is only abated once it is stored, and the pipelines, terminals and permitted stores that get it there are built by other parties on other timetables than the capture plant that depends on them.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 (Net-Zero Industry Act), Art. 20 and 23
World premiere at Heidelberg Materials: Opening of CCS facility in Norway

measures.note: Puts a dated, pro-rata injection-capacity duty on oil and gas entities, which is the only measure in the register that obliges anyone to build the store a capture plant needs.

evidence.quote: Deliver an individual share of the Union's 50 Mt/year CO2 injection capacity target by 2030, calculated pro-rata on the entity's share of Union crude oil and natural gas production over 2020-2023, as permitted capacity available to the market.

measures.note: Third-party access is what makes somebody else's store usable by a cement plant, but it is qualified by economic feasibility.

evidence.quote: Take the measures needed to open access to CO2 transport networks and storage sites for geological storage, as far as it is economically feasible or where a potential customer is willing to pay.

bottlenecks.name: Retrofit cost against plant economics
bottlenecks.description: A capture retrofit costs a large fraction of what the plant it sits on is worth, and the projects that have gone ahead in Europe have all done so with public money in the stack rather than on the plant's own cash flow.

sources.title: Heidelberg Materials pauses Slite CCS project
First fully decarbonised cement plant in Germany: EU Innovation Fund backs Heidelberg Materials' GeZero project with €191 million
Carbon sequestration and reuse — capital and operating cost estimates (archived)

measures.note: The same schedule that improves the case for a retrofit raises the plant's running cost before the retrofit exists, on plants whose margins are what the retrofit has to be financed from.

evidence.quote: Producers of CBAM-covered goods see their free allocation shrink on a fixed annual CBAM-factor schedule, falling to 0% from 2038, as CBAM replaces free allocation as the carbon-leakage instrument for those goods.
evidence.article: Art. 1(15)(b)(i), replacing Art. 10a(1a), second subparagraph of Directive 2003/87/EC

measures.note: Strategic-project recognition shortens permitting and improves access to support, without providing capital.

evidence.quote: File an application for strategic-project recognition containing evidence against the criteria, a business plan evaluating financial viability, and a draft timetable showing when the project contributes to the Union benchmark.

bottlenecks.name: Dependence on revocable public support
bottlenecks.description: Where the business case rests on a national or EU support decision, a change of position by the funder stops the project outright, and it stops it after the engineering is done rather than before it starts.

sources.title: Heidelberg Materials pauses Slite CCS project
Heidelberg Materials withdraws Slite CCS permit application

bottlenecks.name: Green premium against willingness to pay
bottlenecks.description: Captured-carbon cement costs more to make than the cement it replaces, and the buyer of the concrete is usually not the party that carries the climate commitment, so the premium has to be pulled through the chain by procurement rules rather than by demand.

sources.title: Cement and concrete — Breakthrough Agenda Report 2025
Industrial Accelerator Act proposal, lead-market provisions (Annex II)

measures.note: Withdrawing free allocation raises the cost of unabated clinker, which narrows the gap the low-carbon product has to close.

evidence.quote: Producers of CBAM-covered goods see their free allocation shrink on a fixed annual CBAM-factor schedule, falling to 0% from 2038, as CBAM replaces free allocation as the carbon-leakage instrument for those goods.
evidence.article: Art. 1(15)(b)(i), replacing Art. 10a(1a), second subparagraph of Directive 2003/87/EC

measures.note: Procurement rules pull low-carbon concrete through public demand rather than leaving it to willingness to pay.

evidence.quote: Apply the Union-origin and low-carbon requirements laid down in Annex II Part I (steel, concrete/mortar, aluminium) and Annex III Part I (electric vehicles) in covered public procurement.

measures.note: Support schemes carry the same requirements, widening the pull beyond procurement.

evidence.quote: Design public support schemes so that the Union-origin/low-carbon requirements of Annex II Part II and Annex III Part II apply to at least 45% of the national budget for Annex II Part II-type schemes and 100% of the budget for Annex III Part II-type schemes.

measures.note: Same-year certificates stop importers hedging the carbon cost forward, holding imported and domestic carbon costs closer together.

evidence.quote: From 2028, satisfy the quarterly certificate-holding requirement using only certificates bought in the same year, so certificates carried over from earlier years no longer count.
evidence.article: Art. 1(13), adding a subparagraph to Art. 22(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/956

bottlenecks.name: Green premium against willingness to pay
bottlenecks.description: Steel made without a blast furnace costs more than the steel it replaces, and it is sold into construction and vehicle chains where the buyer is several steps removed from whoever carries the climate commitment, so the premium has to be pulled through by procurement and product rules rather than by demand.

sources.title: Steel — Breakthrough Agenda Report 2025
Industrial Accelerator Act proposal, lead-market provisions (Annex II)

measures.note: The one provision in the register that puts a volume share on low-carbon steel by name, which is what turns a premium product into a market rather than a pilot order.

evidence.quote: (a) Steel, and any product the performance of which depends mainly on steel, intended for use in buildings, infrastructure and motor vehicles for civil purposes: at least 25% of the total volume of steel used shall be low-carbon;

measures.note: The duty on the buying side of the same rule: public procurement has to apply the Annex II Part I requirements, and steel is the first product listed there.

evidence.quote: Apply the Union-origin and low-carbon requirements laid down in Annex II Part I (steel, concrete/mortar, aluminium) and Annex III Part I (electric vehicles) in covered public procurement.

measures.note: Withdrawing free allocation raises the cost of blast-furnace steel, which narrows the gap the low-carbon product has to close.

evidence.quote: Producers of CBAM-covered goods see their free allocation shrink on a fixed annual CBAM-factor schedule, falling to 0% from 2038, as CBAM replaces free allocation as the carbon-leakage instrument for those goods.
evidence.article: Art. 1(15)(b)(i), replacing Art. 10a(1a), second subparagraph of Directive 2003/87/EC

measures.note: Support schemes carry the same requirements, widening the pull beyond public contracts.

evidence.quote: Design public support schemes so that the Union-origin/low-carbon requirements of Annex II Part II and Annex III Part II apply to at least 45% of the national budget for Annex II Part II-type schemes and 100% of the budget for Annex III Part II-type schemes.

measures.note: A premium can only be charged for a claim a buyer can check, and this is the provision that makes the low-carbon classification a verified one rather than a marketing term.

evidence.quote: Have emissions and other data used to calculate a product's greenhouse gas intensity verified by accredited verifiers before it can be classified/labelled as low-carbon.

measures.note: Same-year certificates stop importers hedging the carbon cost forward, holding imported and domestic carbon costs closer together.

evidence.quote: From 2028, satisfy the quarterly certificate-holding requirement using only certificates bought in the same year, so certificates carried over from earlier years no longer count.
evidence.article: Art. 1(13), adding a subparagraph to Art. 22(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/956

bottlenecks.name: Conversion cost against site economics
bottlenecks.description: Replacing an integrated site's ironmaking is a rebuild rather than a retrofit, and every European conversion that has gone ahead has done so with public money in the stack. Where the public share was withdrawn or the electricity price moved against it, the conversion stopped.

measures.note: The same schedule that improves the case for converting raises the site's running cost before the conversion exists, on margins the conversion has to be financed from.

evidence.quote: Producers of CBAM-covered goods see their free allocation shrink on a fixed annual CBAM-factor schedule, falling to 0% from 2038, as CBAM replaces free allocation as the carbon-leakage instrument for those goods.
evidence.article: Art. 1(15)(b)(i), replacing Art. 10a(1a), second subparagraph of Directive 2003/87/EC

bottlenecks.name: Renewable hydrogen at volume and at a price
bottlenecks.description: Every direct reduction unit being built in Europe is designed to run on hydrogen and is being commissioned on natural gas, because the hydrogen it would need does not yet arrive in the volume or at the price the iron can carry. The electrolysers, the power contracts and the pipes are built by other parties on other timetables than the furnace that depends on them.

bottlenecks.name: CO2 transport and storage network
bottlenecks.description: The route that keeps an existing blast furnace only counts as abatement once the captured tonne is stored, and the pipelines, terminals and permitted stores that get it there are the same ones the cement sector is waiting for. One network decides whether either sector's capture route works.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1735 (Net-Zero Industry Act), Art. 20 and 23
Successful demonstration in Dunkirk of the CO2 capture DMX process

measures.note: Puts a dated, pro-rata injection-capacity duty on oil and gas entities, which is the only measure in the register that obliges anyone to build the store a capture unit needs.

evidence.quote: Deliver an individual share of the Union's 50 Mt/year CO2 injection capacity target by 2030, calculated pro-rata on the entity's share of Union crude oil and natural gas production over 2020-2023, as permitted capacity available to the market.

measures.note: Third-party access is what makes somebody else's store usable by a steel site, but it is qualified by economic feasibility.

evidence.quote: Take the measures needed to open access to CO2 transport networks and storage sites for geological storage, as far as it is economically feasible or where a potential customer is willing to pay.

bottlenecks.name: Dependence on revocable public support
bottlenecks.description: Where the business case rests on a national support decision, either party can end it. Germany's largest planned conversion ended because the recipient handed the money back rather than because the funder withdrew it, which is the same dependence read from the other side.

sources.title: German finance minister calls steel summit after green projects axed

bottlenecks.name: Scrap supply and quality against electric furnace capacity
bottlenecks.description: The electric furnace route is already two fifths of European output and is the cheapest way to make steel without ironmaking, so what limits it is not the furnace but the scrap: how much Europe collects, how clean it is, and how much of it leaves. Every new furnace announced competes for the same stream.

sources.title: Learn about steel — how steel is made
voestalpine unveils further expansion plans for greentec steel at its Donawitz location

bottlenecks.name: European cells against imported cells
bottlenecks.description: A European gigafactory has to sell cells against imported ones made at larger scale on longer-amortised lines, and the European cost per kWh has not closed that gap. It is the constraint the sector's failures share: the plants that stopped did not stop for want of a market for batteries, they stopped for want of a price at which their own cells cleared.

measures.note: The only provision in the register that puts an origin requirement on battery storage by name, on the buying side. It does not lower a European cost per kWh; it removes part of the demand a cheaper imported cell can compete for.

evidence.quote: Apply the Union-origin requirements laid down in the new Annex II when procuring listed net-zero technologies (battery storage, solar PV, heat pumps, wind, nuclear).

measures.note: The same instrument reaching the cell through the vehicle it sits in rather than through the cell itself, and weighted for that distance: a purchase scheme buys a car, and the origin requirement it applies is a requirement about the car.

evidence.quote: Ensure that only vehicles complying with the Union-origin requirements are eligible under public schemes supporting the purchase, lease, rent or hire-purchase of new electric vehicles.
evidence.article: Art. 12; Art. 13; Annex III, Part II

measures.note: Purchase subsidies have to be designed so that a resilient supply counts, either by paying more for it or by making it the condition of eligibility. It is a criterion rather than a volume, which is why it sits below the procurement rules.

evidence.quote: Design any new or updated scheme that subsidises the purchase of net-zero technology final products so that it favours products with a high sustainability and resilience contribution, either by paying more for them or by making them the eligibility condition.

sources.title: Northvolt files for bankruptcy in Sweden
European ESS battery company Morrow files for bankruptcy

bottlenecks.name: Ramping a cell line to yield
bottlenecks.description: Building a gigafactory and running one are different problems. A cell line reaches its nameplate only when scrap falls far enough for the plant to earn, and the interval between commissioning and that point is where European projects have most often failed. It is a technical constraint with a financial deadline: the capital is spent before the yield arrives.

measures.note: The register reaches the financial deadline on this constraint and not the constraint itself: Innovation Fund money is capital during the interval between commissioning and yield, and three of the sites here hold a grant from its first Battery Call. Nothing in the register reaches scrap rates.

evidence.quote: Grants and other support (e.g. blended finance) from the Innovation Fund, financed by auctioning 200 million allowances from reduced free allocation, are available via open competitive calls for projects scaling up low-/zero-carbon and carbon-negative products, processes and technologies across all Member States.

sources.title: Northvolt files for bankruptcy in Sweden
FREYR Battery, Annual Report on Form 10-K for 2023

bottlenecks.name: Committing capacity against uncertain vehicle demand
bottlenecks.description: A cell factory is sanctioned years before the vehicles it supplies are sold, on a forecast of how fast Europe electrifies. When that forecast moves, the capacity is already half-built. It is the reason given for the largest pauses in the sector, and it is the constraint the fleet CO2 standards act on from the other side — the same rule that makes the demand is what makes the forecast a policy question rather than a commercial one.

measures.note: The one provision that removes the demand question rather than answering it: a 100% reduction on the tailpipe measure means a new car sold in the Union carries a battery, so a factory sanctioned against it is sanctioned against a legal deadline rather than against a forecast.

evidence.quote: Meet an EU fleet-wide target of a 100% reduction on the 2021 baseline for new passenger cars from 2035.

measures.note: The step before it, and the one inside the horizon of a factory being built now — the fleet has to be halfway there five years before the full target bites.

evidence.quote: Meet an EU fleet-wide target of a 55% reduction on the 2021 baseline for new passenger cars, and 50% for new light commercial vehicles.

measures.note: The price of missing the target, which is what turns it from an aspiration into a procurement decision. It is money out of a carmaker rather than money into a cell maker, which is why it is weighted below the targets it enforces.

evidence.quote: Pay an excess emissions premium of EUR 95 per gram per kilometre of exceedance, multiplied by the number of newly registered vehicles.

sources.title: ACC permanently abandons battery projects in Germany and Italy

bottlenecks.name: Cell capacity without the materials behind it
bottlenecks.description: A European cell works still buys most of its cathode and anode material from outside Europe, so onshoring the cell does not by itself onshore the supply chain. The perimeter of this dataset makes the same point from the other direction: cathode, anode, separator and electrolyte works are outside it, and there are very few of them here to hold.

measures.note: The benchmark that answers this constraint directly: extraction, processing and recycling capacity inside the Union for each strategic raw material, which is what a cathode works needs upstream of it. It is a benchmark on the Union rather than a duty on anybody's factory, and it is dated.

evidence.quote: Build Union capacity towards extracting 10%, processing 40% and recycling 25% of the Union's annual consumption of each strategic raw material by 2030.

measures.note: The other half of the same article, and the one that concedes the material will still be imported: it caps how much of it may come from any one country rather than moving the supply into Europe.

evidence.quote: Diversify imports so that no single third country supplies more than 65% of the Union's annual consumption of any strategic raw material by 2030.

measures.note: The route by which a particular materials project gets built: recognition brings shortened permitting and access to finance to the works that would sit upstream of these sites.

evidence.quote: File a Strategic Project application carrying ten items: evidence against the criteria, a UN Framework Classification, a permitting timetable, a public-acceptance plan, ownership and control information, a business plan, a jobs and skills estimate, a post-exploitation environmental restoration plan, an alternative-locations assessment in protected areas, and an indigenous-peoples consultation plan.
